summary.primary_break: K runtime can call configured provider URLs, but outputs are not consistently normalized, persisted into canonical K objects, reviewed, or handed off downstream.

as_built: POST /k/serp/search resolves a serp key through the execution gate and performs urlopen POST to the configured provider URL.
It parses organic_results/results/items and stores provider output on KProductKnowledgeResearchRun.
POST /k/keyword-research/start does not call the provider; it creates a queued run only.
gaps: Keyword research trigger is not a real research pipeline.
SERP results do not populate the keyword table.
There is no async worker to move queued research runs to running/succeeded.

as_built: POST /k/products/{product_id}/enrich/deepseek resolves key alias deepseek and posts product JSON to the configured provider URL.
The result is stored on product.deepseek_structured_output_json and an AI event row.
gaps: No code verifies that the configured URL is actually DeepSeek.
No DeepSeek prompt template, prompt version, model selection, or schema normalization layer is present in K runtime.
Structured output is not mapped into canonical product fields.

as_built: DeepSeek enrichment stores raw structured output and an event.
Risk filter stores risk terms from provider output.
Selling-points endpoint returns a validated response to frontend.
gaps: DeepSeek output is not merged into product attributes or product canonical fields.
SERP keywords are not persisted as keyword candidates.
No single orchestration endpoint runs product creation -> AI -> SERP -> risk -> export.

as_built: Provider requests include task markers such as deepseek_enrichment, bilingual_translation, risk_filtering, and selling_points.
Provider output is returned to caller and, for some endpoints, persisted.
gaps: No explicit prompt construction service is used by K runtime.
No output schema is enforced for DeepSeek enrichment, translation, or risk filtering beyond loose dict parsing.
No prompt_version is written although AIEvent has a prompt_version column.
No product review workflow consumes prompt outputs.

as_built: K router itself does direct HTTP provider calls instead of returning local fake data.
Core adapter metadata declares K action execution_type as no_op.
Core execution provider contracts for K providers are executable=false and can_request_execution=false.
K15/K16 frontend text and states still describe future/trigger behavior in places.
gaps: Adapter and execution provider registry do not match runtime behavior.
Registered provider contracts are not executable provider dispatchers.
No tests prove live provider execution success for K endpoints.

blocking_ai_gaps: No canonical AI normalization and field merge layer for DeepSeek output.
No closed orchestration pipeline across DeepSeek, SERP, keyword persistence, risk review, and downstream export.
No prompt versioning or strict schema validation for most K AI calls.
No direct K endpoint tests for provider execution behavior were found.
